title: Problem Overview and Imports
content: The file formalizes Erdos Problem #980 on the sum of least $k$-th power nonresidues over primes. It imports Mathlib modules for prime number basics, the Legendre symbol, asymptotics, and logarithmic functions. The `open Nat Real` command brings natural number and real number notations into scope.
mathContext: The problem asks whether $\sum_{p < x} n_k(p) \sim c_k \cdot x/\log x$ where $n_k(p)$ is the least $k$-th power nonresidue modulo prime $p$. This connects the distribution of power residues to prime counting asymptotics via $\pi(x) \sim x/\log x$.

title: k-th Power Residue
content: An integer $a$ is a $k$-th power residue mod $p$ if $a \equiv b^k \pmod{p}$ for some integer $b$. For $k = 2$, these are the classical quadratic residues. The set of $k$-th power residues forms a subgroup of $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$ of index $\gcd(k, p-1)$, so roughly $1/k$ of nonzero residues are $k$-th power residues when $k \mid (p-1)$.
mathContext: $\text{IsPowerResidue}(k, p, a) :\iff \exists b,\; b^k \equiv a \pmod{p}$. The $k$-th power residues form a subgroup $H \leq (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^*$ with $[(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^* : H] = \gcd(k, p-1)$.

title: k-th Power Nonresidue
content: An integer $a$ is a $k$-th power nonresidue mod $p$ if it is not a $k$-th power residue and $a \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$. The condition $a \% p \neq 0$ excludes multiples of $p$, which are neither residues nor nonresidues in the classical sense.

title: Quadratic Case Equivalence
content: For $k = 2$, the general power nonresidue definition specializes to quadratic nonresidues: $a$ is a quadratic nonresidue mod $p$ iff $\nexists b,\; b^2 \equiv a \pmod{p}$ and $a \not\equiv 0 \pmod{p}$. The Legendre symbol characterizes this: $(a/p) = -1$ for nonresidues.
mathContext: $\text{IsPowerNonresidue}(2, p, a) \iff (\nexists b,\; b^2 \equiv a \pmod{p}) \wedge p \nmid a$. Equivalently, the Legendre symbol $(a/p) = -1$.

title: Least Power Nonresidue
content: The least $k$-th power nonresidue $n_k(p) = \min\{a \geq 1 : a \text{ is a } k\text{-th power nonresidue mod } p\}$. This is the central quantity in Erdos's problem. The definition uses `Nat.find` to select the smallest witness, returning 0 if no nonresidue exists (which cannot happen for primes $p > k$).
mathContext: $n_k(p) = \min\{a \in \mathbb{N} : a \geq 1 \wedge a \text{ is a } k\text{-th power NR mod } p\}$. The sequence $n_2(p)$ for primes $p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, \ldots$ starts $2, 2, 3, 2, 2, \ldots$

title: Existence of Quadratic Nonresidues
content: For any odd prime $p$, quadratic nonresidues exist: exactly half of the nonzero residues mod $p$ are quadratic residues and half are nonresidues. This axiom guarantees the least nonresidue function is well-defined for $p > 2$.

title: Vinogradov's Bound
content: Vinogradov's classical bound on the least quadratic nonresidue: $n(p) = O(p^{1/(4\sqrt{e}) + \varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon > 0$. The exponent $1/(4\sqrt{e}) \approx 0.1516$ comes from deep character sum estimates. This was later improved by Burgess (1962) using his celebrated short character sum inequality.
mathContext: $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\; \exists C > 0,\; \forall p \text{ prime},\; n_2(p) \leq C \cdot p^{1/(4\sqrt{e}) + \varepsilon}$. The Burgess bound refines this: $n(p) \ll p^{1/(4\sqrt{e}) + \varepsilon}$.

title: GRH Bound
content: Under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, the least quadratic nonresidue satisfies $n(p) = O((\log p)^2)$. This conditional bound is dramatically better than the unconditional Vinogradov/Burgess bounds, showing the least nonresidue is very small relative to $p$. The proof uses explicit formulas connecting character sums to zeros of $L$-functions.
mathContext: $\text{GRH} \implies \exists C > 0,\; \forall p \text{ prime},\; n_2(p) \leq C (\log p)^2$. Compared to the unconditional $n(p) \leq p^{0.1516+\varepsilon}$, this is exponentially better.

title: Sum of Least Nonresidues $S_k(x)$
content: The sum $S_k(x) = \sum_{p < x,\; p \text{ prime}} n_k(p)$ aggregates the least $k$-th power nonresidues over all primes below $x$. The formalization uses `Finset.range` with a primality filter. This is the main object of study in Problem #980.
mathContext: $S_k(x) = \sum_{\substack{p < x \\ p \text{ prime}}} n_k(p)$. The problem asks whether $S_k(x) \sim c_k \cdot x/\log x$ as $x \to \infty$.

title: The Constant $c_2$
content: The explicit constant in the quadratic case: $c_2 = \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} p_j / 2^j$ where $p_j$ is the $j$-th prime. This series converges because primes grow like $j \log j$ (by the prime number theorem) while the denominator $2^j$ grows exponentially. The partial sums give $c_2 = 2/2 + 3/4 + 5/8 + 7/16 + 11/32 + \cdots \approx 3.67$.
mathContext: $c_2 = \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} \frac{p_j}{2^j} = \frac{2}{2} + \frac{3}{4} + \frac{5}{8} + \frac{7}{16} + \cdots$. Satisfies $3.5 < c_2 < 4$. The convergence follows from $p_j \sim j \log j$ and the ratio test.

title: General Constants $c_k$
content: For $k \geq 2$, the constant $c_k$ in the asymptotic $\sum n_k(p) \sim c_k \cdot x/\log x$ is defined via character sums and the distribution of $k$-th power residues. The exact formula involves a weighted sum over primes analogous to $c_2$, but with weights depending on the $k$-th power residue structure. Positivity is axiomatized via `c_k_positive`.
mathContext: $c_k > 0$ for all $k \geq 2$. The formula generalizes $c_2 = \sum p_j/2^j$ to higher power residue characters. The positivity follows from the fact that $k$-th power nonresidues exist among small integers for all primes $p > k$.

title: Erdos's Result (1961)
content: Erdos proved the quadratic case ($k = 2$) in his 1961 paper 'Remarks on number theory I' (Mat. Lapok): $\sum_{p<x} n_2(p) \sim c_2 \cdot x/\log x$. The asymptotic is stated in two equivalent forms: absolute error ($|S_2(x) - c_2 x/\log x| < \varepsilon \cdot x/\log x$) and ratio convergence ($S_2(x)/(x/\log x) \to c_2$). The proof uses properties of the Legendre symbol and the prime number theorem.
mathContext: $\sum_{p < x} n_2(p) = c_2 \cdot \frac{x}{\log x} + o\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right)$ where $c_2 = \sum_{j \geq 1} p_j/2^j \approx 3.67$.

title: Elliott's Generalization (1967)
content: P.D.T.A. Elliott extended Erdos's result from $k = 2$ to all $k \geq 2$ in his 1967 paper 'A problem of Erdos concerning power residue sums' (Acta Arithmetica, 131-149). This completely solved Problem #980. Elliott's proof generalizes the character sum techniques to $k$-th power residue characters, using the Polya-Vinogradov inequality for higher-order characters.
mathContext: $\forall k \geq 2,\; \sum_{p<x} n_k(p) = c_k \cdot \frac{x}{\log x} + o\left(\frac{x}{\log x}\right)$ with $c_k > 0$.

title: Main Solution Theorem
content: The main theorem: for $k \geq 2$, there exists $c > 0$ such that $\sum_{p<x} n_k(p) \sim c \cdot x/\log x$. The proof instantiates $c = c_k(k)$, uses `c_k_positive` for positivity, and `elliott_1967_general` for the asymptotic. This is a constructive combination of the axiomatized results.
mathContext: $\forall k \geq 2,\; \exists c > 0,\; |S_k(x) - c \cdot x/\log x| < \varepsilon \cdot x/\log x$ for all $x \geq x_0(\varepsilon)$.

title: Average and Typical Size
content: The average value of $n_k(p)$ over primes $p < x$ is approximately $c_k \cdot \log x$, since $\pi(x) \sim x/\log x$. While individual values can be as large as $O(p^{0.15+\varepsilon})$ (Vinogradov), the average is only $O(\log x)$. This shows that large nonresidues are rare among primes — most primes have small least nonresidues.
mathContext: $\frac{1}{\pi(x)} \sum_{p < x} n_k(p) \sim c_k \cdot \log x$ as $x \to \infty$, since $\pi(x) \sim x/\log x$.

title: Special Cases: $n_2(p) = 2$ and $n_2(p) = 3$
content: The least quadratic nonresidue is 2 for infinitely many primes — precisely those with $p \equiv 3, 5 \pmod{8}$ (by the second supplement to quadratic reciprocity). Similarly, $n_2(p) = 3$ for infinitely many primes where 2 is a QR but 3 is not, occurring for $p \equiv 1, 7 \pmod{24}$. By Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions, each residue class contains infinitely many primes.

title: Polya-Vinogradov Connection
content: The Polya-Vinogradov inequality bounds partial sums of Dirichlet characters: $|\sum_{n \leq N} \chi(n)| \leq C\sqrt{p} \log p$. This is the key analytic tool underlying both Erdos's and Elliott's proofs, as it controls the distribution of $k$-th power residue symbols over intervals, enabling precise estimates of how often $n_k(p)$ takes various values.
mathContext: The Polya-Vinogradov inequality (1918): $|\sum_{n=1}^{N} \chi(n)| \leq c \sqrt{q} \log q$ for any non-principal character $\chi \pmod{q}$. This is used to show that power residues are well-distributed in short intervals.
